_comment: 🔮️ Test-only references of the quiz product (Protocol v2). Every case under ../🧪️tests names one of these oracles; the TypeScript twin (@semio-tech/quiz) and the Rust twin (semio-framework-quiz) are the subjects and are additionally held to each other. The Python references live inside the case adapters (🧪️tests/*/🐍️.py) and are written from the design text only. Shared vectors under ../🧫️fixtures are generated from those same adapters, so a committed vector and its oracle can never disagree; the generation command is stated in every feature.

oracles.rationale: The quiz randomness contract (design §3) is MT19937 seeded with init_genrand and read as tempered u32 words, plus FNV-1a seeds, rejection-sampled uniform indices and a Fisher–Yates shuffle over that stream. numpy's MT19937 bit generator is the reference stream: RandomState(seed) runs init_genrand for a scalar seed and the state is handed to MT19937.random_raw unchanged. The case additionally loads CPython's own random.Random — an unrelated MT19937 implementation — with the same 624-word state and requires the same words, and pins the C++ standard's check value (the 10000th word of a default-seeded std::mt19937 is 4123659995, [rand.predef]). Surveyed and declined: seedrandom (ARC4/xor families, no MT19937), pure-rand (its MT19937 is not exposed as raw tempered words with init_genrand seeding across versions), jstat (no PRNG). FNV-1a, uniform and shuffle are derived in the adapter from the design text and consume only the library's words.

packages.role: Vectorised pair matrices (subtract.outer, greater.outer, sign) and pairwise summation for the weighted concordance cross-check.

oracles.rationale: Scoring (design §6) is a magnitude-weighted pair concordance for sorting and matching and a profile-distance credit for classification. No library implements the magnitude weights — they are this product's policy — so the oracle adapters compute the projected score with the design's pair loop and refuse to project it unless two independent evaluations agree within 1e-12: numpy over the full pair matrix (unrelated evaluation and summation order), and scipy.stats.kendalltau for the unit-weight reading of the same engine, where the score is (1 + τ_a)/2 over the pairs the truth orders and τ_a follows from scipy's τ_b and the tie counts. Classification distances and d_max are recomputed with scipy.spatial.distance.euclidean and pdist. Surveyed and declined: jstat (no Kendall τ with tie handling), simple-statistics (not in the lockfile, no tie-corrected τ_b).

The contract 🧬️schema/🔣️.json is JSON Schema draft-07 and normative; the product validates quizzes and catalogs with its own structural and semantic validator (quizIssues, catalogIssues) and deliberately links no schema library at runtime. python-jsonschema's Draft7Validator reads the normative file itself and judges every quiz and catalog the product meets — the committed vectors, the authored teaching content and a set of rejected documents that each break one named rule — so the owned validator is held to the schema rather than to its own reading of it. It also validates every other schema-typed document in the committed vectors (sheets, answers, results, commands, events, views) and fails the oracle phase on any violation. ajv (already in the lockfile) was the alternative; the Python host was chosen so the conformance oracle sits beside the other Python references of this owner. For shared presence (design §15) it judges every committed PresenceState and CursorState at its boundaries (tag, anchor, coordinates in [0, 1], undeclared members); the place rules the schema cannot state (a run or its results names its quiz, only a run names a task) and the room scopes are written beside it in the case adapter from the design text. For the id shapes and the handle policy (case 🪪️identity-shapes) it judges every committed command and query against `Command` and `Query` (`Id`, `Slug`) and every normalized handle against `$defs/Handle`, whose pattern is the handle alphabet; the adapter holds the validator itself to the Unicode Character Database through CPython's `unicodedata` — the alphabet the pattern admits over every Unicode scalar value must be exactly the Latin letters the database derives (general category Lu or Ll in five blocks, no compatibility decomposition) plus digits, space and four punctuation marks, every member an NFC-stable starter and every admitted display its own NFC form — and takes the lowercase key from Python's `str.lower`, an implementation of the Unicode case mappings unrelated to the ICU of the TypeScript runtime and to Rust's tables. Surveyed and declined for normalization: the `idna` package of the lockfile (it checks IDNA labels, whose alphabet and mapping rules differ) and `unicodedata2` (not in the lockfile; the standard library's data is the same database).

packages.role: The MT19937 stream every sheet is drawn from.

engine.implementation: in-repository second implementation of design §3–§8, written in Python from the design text

oracles.rationale: Sheet assembly, answer validity, badge rules, the leaderboard's tie-break chain and the learner lifecycle are this product's own policy: no third party implements them, and a survey of the Python, JavaScript and Rust ecosystems (quiz engines such as H5P, Moodle's question engine and Open edX's capa problems score per question with their own rubrics and randomise with platform RNGs) found nothing that could state these outcomes. The reference is therefore a second implementation written in Python from the design text only, never from the TypeScript or Rust twins, drawing sheets from numpy's MT19937. It is registered as a cross-semio implementation — a supplement, never third-party evidence — and it is not the only check: both twins are also held to each other by the harness's pairwise subject parity, so every one of these cases compares three independently written readings of the design. The crowd view (design §17) is aggregation policy too; its reference recounts every count with collections.Counter and recomputes every mean position with numpy.mean before projecting. The four leaderboards count the runs of a calendar window in UTC — the day, the ISO week, the month around an instant — and which run counts is policy, but where a day, a week and a month begin is not: the reference reads every window off CPython's `datetime` (date arithmetic, `weekday`, month replacement), a calendar implementation unrelated to the days-from-civil arithmetic both twins carry, over instants at the epoch, year ends, leap days — also those that end a 400-year era — and the February of a common century.

Judges the sorting score inside the unit suite `🧪️tests/⚖️partial-credit-scoring` of @semio-tech/quiz (vitest, devDependency of the core package). With equally spaced values on a linear scale the magnitude weights are rank differences, and the weighted pair concordance then equals (1 + ρ)/2 with Spearman's ρ — so jStat.spearmancoeff states the score of every permutation the suite draws (n = 2…15) within 1e-12. This is the rank reading of design §6; the Kendall reading with unit weights is judged by quiz-scipy-stats in the Protocol v2 case.

Judges the profile distances d and d_max of the classification credit inside the unit suite `🧪️tests/⚖️partial-credit-scoring` of @semio-tech/quiz (vitest, devDependency of the core package): math.distance over the normalised profiles must reproduce every distance the owned credit uses. scipy.spatial.distance is the corresponding reference of the Protocol v2 case (quiz-scipy-stats).

Judges the owned structural validator inside the unit suite `🧪️tests/🩺️document-validation` of @semio-tech/quiz (vitest, devDependency of the core package): ajv compiles the normative 🧬️schema/🔣️.json and, for every tested quiz and catalog document, accepts it exactly when quizIssues/catalogIssues report no structural issue. It is the JavaScript engine beside python-jsonschema (quiz-jsonschema), which judges the same contract in the Protocol v2 case — two independent schema engines.

Judges the owned radar (spider diagram) geometry of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🕷️radar-geometry` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): every axis value maps to its radius by d3-scale's scaleLinear with clamping over the axis [min, max], for 3 to 9 axes (252 points), and the owned renderer must place the same points. The renderer itself links no chart library.

Judges the owned radar label layout of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🕷️radar-geometry` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): opentype.js parses the site's brand font and measures real glyph advances, and every wrapped axis label box the owned renderer lays out must stay inside the chart at phone, tablet and desktop widths. The renderer itself measures with an owned width estimate and links no font library.

engine.implementation: lightningcss transform() with a StyleSheet visitor over its parsed media queries and grid track lists

oracles.rationale: Judges the home grid of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🏠️home-grid` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): lightningcss — the CSS engine Tailwind itself runs the site's styles through — parses the renderer's stylesheet into media queries, grid track lists and variables, and the tracks the card layer takes at 320 to 1440 px (one column below tablets, the overview's `--layered-columns`/`--layered-rows` from there, no gap or padding between tracks, the spacing inside `.quiz-home-cell`) and the breakpoints themselves must equal the shared vectors and the design system's `UI_MOBILE_MAX_WIDTH_PX` / `UI_TABLET_MAX_WIDTH_PX`; it also parses the overview's own track lists into fr weights that must equal the shared weights of each layout (1 : 1.5 : 1 by 1 : 1.4 : 1 on desktops). jsdom lays nothing out and evaluates no media query (the width is emulated through `matchMedia`), so the stylesheet's own parse is the independent reading; the two-device walk in a real browser confirms the same grid.

engine.implementation: lodash/throttle with leading and trailing edges

oracles.rationale: Judges the presence frame throttle of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/📡️presence-client` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): for every shared call schedule whose states are pairwise distinct, the frames a presence room sends (time and state, under fake timers) must equal the invocations of lodash's throttle with the same interval — the reference leading-and-trailing-edge throttle. Schedules that repeat a state are judged by the shared vectors alone, since the room never resends the state it sent last. The drafts a thinking room sends (at most every 500 ms) must be the drafts lodash's throttle invokes with the same interval, each sent no later than lodash's (the room times from its last frame, lodash from its timer).

engine.implementation: lodash/groupBy, lodash/orderBy, lodash/sortBy, lodash/mean and lodash/round

oracles.rationale: Judges what the others think as @semio-tech/quiz-react shows it, inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/💭️crowd-client` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): for every shared vector, the choices of a live item recomputed by lodash straight from the others' raw drafts (grouped by category or value, tags sorted, ordered by count descending, then numerically, then by code point) and the choices of a submitted item reordered by lodash from the crowd view's code point ordered counts must equal the client's; the mean of a live item's positions must equal lodash's mean, and every place lodash's rounding to one decimal of `1 + position × (total − 1)`.

engine.implementation: colord with its a11y plugin: `contrast()` (WCAG 2 relative luminance contrast) over colours given as HSL

oracles.rationale: Judges the ink of another learner's name label of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🌗️contrast-states` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): for each of the 48 palette slots of the shared vector and both appearances, the contrast colord's a11y plugin computes between the ink the renderer chose (`peerInk`) and the slot colour of the design system's presence palette (`presenceColor`, converted from HSL by colord itself) must reach 4.5 : 1 (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3). The renderer links no colour library: it converts HSL to sRGB and takes the WCAG relative luminance itself to choose black or white. Surveyed and declined: `color` (in node_modules but not in the lockfile, no types), `d3-color` (no contrast function), `culori` (needs a separate types package).

engine.implementation: aria-query `roles` map: the WAI-ARIA 1.2 role model with each role's implicit property values

oracles.rationale: Judges which elements of @semio-tech/quiz-react speak by themselves inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/📢️live-regions` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): an element is a live region by its own `aria-live` or by the implicit `aria-live` aria-query's role model gives its role (`status` polite, `alert` assertive). For every step of the shared vector, in both languages, the connection indicator and all its ancestors must be silent by that model, exactly one element must be live, and it must hold the vector's announcement. aria-query is the role model @testing-library/dom itself queries with; the suite reads it directly so that the verdict does not depend on the renderer's own notion of a live region.

engine.implementation: i18next language utilities: `getBestMatchFromCodes` with `supportedLngs`, `nonExplicitSupportedLngs`, `cleanCode` and no fallback language

oracles.rationale: Judges the language a browser's list preselects in @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🌍️language-choice` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): for every browser language list of the shared vector, a fresh i18next instance configured with the offered languages and `fallbackLng: false` must negotiate the same language as the renderer's `preferredLocale` — and none where the vector says none, which is what makes the renderer ask instead of assuming a language. The renderer's own negotiation is a few lines over the primary language subtag and links nothing; i18next is otherwise used by the repo's shared i18n port, where the quiz always names its language explicitly.

engine.implementation: jsdom `History` over the session history of a window of its own: `pushState`, `replaceState` and `go` (WHATWG HTML, the History interface)

oracles.rationale: Judges the trail of @semio-tech/quiz-react inside its unit suite `🧪️tests/🚏️navigation` (vitest, devDependency of the react package): every trail of the shared vector that closes no run is replayed on the session history of a fresh jsdom window — a step opened is pushed, a step entered on arrival replaces the entry, back and forward traverse — and after every move the step in front and the steps one entry behind and ahead (read by going there and back) must be the ones the renderer's own trail answers (`stepBefore`, `stepAfter`). The renderer keeps its trail itself and writes no entry into the browser's history (the address is replaced in place); jsdom is otherwise only the suite's environment. Trails in which a run closes have no counterpart in a browser's history — a closed run leaves the trail — and are held to the shared vector alone.

comparisonProfiles.description: Structural identity with the quiz scoring parity tolerance of 1e-12 (design §6): log10 may differ by one ulp between language runtimes. Ids, kinds, orders and every non-numeric field still compare exactly.

subjectFeatures.rationale: 🧪️ The quiz crate re-exports its JSON codec (serde_json) only under `sut`, so the Rust subject adapters can decode the shared vectors into the typed twins and encode their answers, while production builds of the crate stay free of it.

oracleHostPackages.rationale: 🌀️ MT19937 stream of the randomness oracle and of every Python reference that draws a sheet; pair matrices of the scoring cross-checks.
📊️ Kendall τ and Euclidean distances of the scoring cross-checks.
🧬️ Draft 7 validation of every quiz document against the normative schema.
